correctness.rationale: The crown distance table has only matched opposite vertices at distance three. Hence every selected set of size at least three satisfies the semitotal witness condition, and domination reduces to exact occupancy cases. The counting formula follows from disjoint occupancy classes. Inclusion-minimality is verified by one-vertex deletion and yields only the two sides, matched-index triples, and disjoint-index two-plus-two sets. A direct checker verifies all vertex subsets for n=3 through 7 and matches both polynomials.

value.rationale: Upper semitotal domination is defined through inclusion-minimal semitotal dominating sets, so a complete description of those sets is structurally central. The result additionally gives the entire semitotal domination polynomial on a standard regular bipartite family, exact minimal-size counts, and a direct explanation of how the known upper scalar bound is attained.
